These Olympic days seem to get busier and busier.
It’s been wall-to-wall thrills and spills yet again, finishing with Chinese weightlifting golds and drama on the athletics track in the men’s 400m and 3000m steeplechase.
There is no let-up for the rest of the Games, so let’s all rest up then come back for more tomorrow.
As ever, the Post will be here to bring you it, so join us then.
Happy ending?
The reallocated medals from the team figure skating marred by doping at the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics are finally around the necks of their new owners.
In a ceremony by the Eiffel Tower, the United States and Japan were awarded gold and silver respectively, a mere 2½ years after that saga began.
At the time, gold was won by Russia, with a team including Kamila Valieva.
It emerged that Valieva, then 15, had tested positive before the Games for trimetazidine – yes, the heart drug for which 23 Chinese swimmers tested positive before being cleared in 2021.
Valieva is serving a four-year ban for doping and the team figure skating scores now exclude her share of Russia’s total.
A medal ceremony did not take place in Beijing, and in any case would have been sparsely attended because of Covid-19 restrictions.
The nine-strong American and Japanese teams had an audience of 13,000 fans at Champions Park in Paris instead.
There’s been a gold for China in artistic swimming, the sport that changed its name from synchronised swimming.
It’s the country’s first triumph in the acrobatic team event.
This discipline is normally dominated by Russia, who are excluded from these Games.
That leaves China to win with 996.1389 points, well clear of the United States, who take silver with 914.3421, and Spain, who win bronze with 900.7319.
Wearing wearing red sequined swimsuits, the Chinese team tossed a swimmer high into the air during their routine, named “Light of Life”.
Uzbekistan boxer Bakhodir Jalolov will battle Ayoub Ghadfa of Spain in the final of the men’s over-92kg division – that’s super-heavyweight.
Reigning champion Jalolov defeats Nelvie Tiafack of Germany by unanimous decision for a third 5-0 win in as many bouts.
Ghadfa also wins by unanimous decision against France’s Djamili-Dini Aboudou Moindze.
In the women’s basketball quarter-finals, the United States have defeated Nigeria 88-74.
A’ja Wilson leads the scoring with 20 points, while Jackie Young contributes 15.
That is 59 Olympic wins in a row for the Americans, who have not been beaten since the Barcelona Games in 1992.
They are two victories from an eighth consecutive gold.
Next up for them are Australia in Friday’s semi-final.
Some last action from the Stade de France, where Morocco’s Soufiane El Bakkali has become the first man in 88 years to retain a 3,000 metres steeplechase crown.
He overtook Kenneth Rooks of the United States on the final straight after a dramatic last lap in which Lamecha Girma, the world record-holder from Ethiopia, hit a hurdle and fell heavily.
Girma was later carried from the track on a stretcher.
El Bakkali matched the feat of Finland’s Volmari Iso Hollo in 1932 and 1936.
And there was women’s pole vault gold for Australia after Nina Kennedy cleared a season’s best 4.90 metres to beat her American rival Katie Moon.
Polish boxer Julia Szeremeta will fight Chinese Taipei’s Lin Yu-ting in the women’s 57kg final after dispatching Philippines boxer Nesthy Petecio in convincing style.
Tokyo Games silver medallist Petecio is in control in the first round but the 20-year-old Szeremeta turns the bout in her favour in the second round before dominating in the third to seal a 4-1 win.
Greek pole vaulter Eleni-Klaoudia Polak was disqualified from the Olympics and handed a provisional suspension after she tested positive for banned substances, the IOC said on Wednesday.
The Greek Olympic Committee said on Tuesday that one member of its team was expelled from the athletes’ village but her identity was previously unknown.
Polak cleared a height of 4.20 metres in the qualification round but did not reach Wednesday’s final.
She was listed as “DQ” in the results.
Chinese Taipei boxer Lin Yu-ting advances to the women’s 57-kg final after securing a unanimous decision win over Esra Yildiz of Turkey in the first of two semi-finals at Roland Garros.
None of the five judges award any of the three rounds to Yildiz as the 28-year-old Lin secures her third 5-0 victory in the French capital in as many bouts.
Hou’s arms failed her on her first attempt at 117kg.
Minutes later, she strode back to the stage and, after audibly rousing herself, performed a beautifully controlled lift to break the Olympic record and retain her crown.
It was the last lift of the competition and earned Hou the title by the narrowest of margins.
Hou’s final total is 206kg, with Cambei relegated to silver despite managing 205kg.
Bronze goes to Thailand’s Khambao, who lifted a combined 200kg.
Mihaela Cambei wildly shakes her clenched fists after somehow steadying herself under 112kg and remaining stationary to receive the green light.
Hou Zhihui needs an Olympic record 117kg lift on her final attempt to retain the title she won in Tokyo.
And the venue erupts as Hou does it, claiming gold in the most dramatic style.
Who knew there were so many Chinese spectators inside South Paris Arena 6?
Hou is involved in a thrilling battle for weightlifting gold.
She moves level with Cambei after lifting 110kg, only for the Romanian to replicate that effort and open up a narrow overall lead.
Surodchana Khambao of Thailand is part of this argument, too.
Her total from the two disciplines is 198kg.
Hou has lifted a combined 199kg, while Cambei’s tally is 203kg.
Hockey glee for China.
Their dream Olympic run will go all the way to a gold medal match against world No 1 team the Netherlands on Friday.
The Chinese lead for 41 minutes of their semi-final against Belgium following an 18th-minute goal from Zou Meirong.
Emma Puvrez equalises with only 60 seconds remaining, but China dust themselves down to win a shootout 3-2.
The final will be staged under the Friday night lights of Yves-du-Manoir Stadium in Paris.
It starts at 2am on Saturday, Hong Kong time.
Whatever the result, that is another medal added to the Chinese tally.
China’s Zhu Yaming is through to the men’s triple jump final.
His compatriots Su Wen or Fang Yaoqing do not make it, and nor do Kim Jang-woo of South Korea nor India’s Praveen Chithravel and Abdulla Narangolintevida.
Pedro Pichardo, the Cuban-born Portuguese who won gold in Tokyo, jumps furthest with 17.44 metres.
Chinese Taipei’s Fang Wan-ling very briefly claims top spot over here at an excitable South Paris Arena 6 weightlifting venue.
She hoists 102kg in the clean and jerk.
Fang is promptly overhauled, though.
Accompanied by shouts of “through the roof” from one of her coaching team, the USA’s Jourdan Delacruz lifts 105kg.
Halfway leader Cambei goes one better, and hoiks 106kg into the air.
At the Stade de France, the men’s 400 metres final is quite something.
Quincy Hall of the US surges from way back to catch runaway leader Matthew Hudson-Smith on the line.
Hall clocks 43.40 seconds, leaning just ahead of the Briton in 43.44.
Those are the fourth and fifth fastest times ever.
Only the illustrious Wayde Van Niekerk, Michael Johnson and Butch Reynolds have run quicker.
AJ, Klitschko, Lewis and?
Four men’s fights will follow the opening two women’s bouts.
There are the two over-92kg semi-finals.
That’s the super-heavyweight category won at past Games by Anthony Joshua (2012), Wladimir Klitschko (1996) and Lennox Lewis (1988).
After that, it’s the 63.5kg final then the 80kg final.
At Roland Garros, six bouts across four weigh classes are coming up.
Chinese Taipei’s Lin Yu-ting will face Esra Yildiz of Turkey in the first of two women’s 57kg semi-finals from 3.30am.
In the centre of a sex eligibility row, Lin has won both her fights in Paris by unanimous decisions and the 28-year-old has said her target is to win the gold medal.
The Philippines’ Nesthy Petecio, the Tokyo Olympics silver medallist, fights in the second semi.
She takes on Poland’s Julia Szeremeta, who knocked out second seed Tina Rahimi of Australia in the round of 16.
Hou is unable to pull off her 93kg attempt.
She is poised to go into the clean and jerk phase in second, behind Romania’s Mihaela Cambei, who releases a tribal roar after she does pick up 93kg of steel and iron.
An intriguing footnote to those men’s 200m semi-finals.
Winner of the third semi, and through to the final at 2.30am tomorrow Hong Kong time, is Erriyon Knighton.
This is the US sprinter who was cleared to race in Paris after his positive test for the anabolic steroid Trenbolone was attributed to the 20-year-old eating contaminated meat.

China’s anti-doping body Chinada has said his case exposes hypocrisy in pointing the finger at the Chinese swimmers who were cleared to compete in Tokyo and Paris after testing positive for trimetazidine, or TMZ.
Hou Zhihui is aiming to follow in the footsteps of fellow Chinese Li Fabin and retain an Olympic weightlifting title.
The 27-year-old is defending her 49kg crown from Tokyo.
It is a dodgy start for Hou.
She records a no-lift on her first attempt at 89kg, but quickly atones with a flawless second go.
“Stick another few kilos on there,” she indicates.
Hou will be back to have a bash at 93kg.
Noah Lyles remains on track to attempt a sprint double at these Games as he reaches the final of the 200 metres.
Letsile Tebogo of Botswana is first in their second of three semi-finals in 19.96 to qualify fastest, with Lyles coasting behind him in 20.08, which is the round’s third fastest time.
Between them is Kenny Bednarek, his fellow American, who wins the first semi in 20.00.
Andre De Grasse of Canada, the champion in Tokyo three years ago, is out.
So too is Wayde van Niekerk of South Africa, the 2016 gold medallist over 400 metres.
China’s Li Fabin has been speaking to the Post after winning repeat weightlifting gold.
He talks about being on “a mission for my country” and says he was so moved by the support he received in France that he may not retire as previously hinted.
Hockey shock?
China take the lead in a tense women’s hockey semi-final with Belgium.
There is no score after the first quarter, as the Chinese aim to spring another shock after toppling Australia in their last-eight tie two days ago.
Then they break the deadlock through Zou Meirong after 18 minutes.
The winners will face the Netherlands, after a 3-0 semi-final success for the world No 1 side against Argentina, the team ranked No 2.
Xu Zhuoyi of China goes in the third men’s 110m hurdles semi.

This is the guy who has won over fans at home with his charmingly “nerdy” look, running in spectacles and prompting people to quip that he took the wrong flight and was meant to be at the Maths Olympiad.
Orlando Bennett of Jamaica wins in 13.09 seconds, with Xu seventh in 13.48.
So that’s the end of the road for Xu, but he’s brought a lot of pleasure along the way.
Qin Weibo also bows out, but Japan’s Rachid Muratake makes it into the final.
The action continues at the Stade de France, where there’s plenty of track and field to come.
Later are semi-finals in the men’s 400m hurdles (1.35am), men’s 200m (2.02am) and women’s 400m (2.45am).
It all culminates in the men’s 400m final at 3.20am.
But first, the three semi-finals of the men’s 110 metres hurdles.
Grant Holloway wins the first semi comfortably, clocking 12.98 seconds.
Qin Weibo of China is sixth in 13.41.
Australia’s Olympic hockey player Tom Craig was released from police custody and apologised, after being arrested in Paris on Wednesday.
A police union source said earlier Craig was being held for buying cocaine.
“I’d firstly like to apologise for what has occurred in the last 24 hours.
I made a terrible mistake.
I take full responsibility for my actions,” Craig said as he left police offices.
“My actions are my own and in no way reflect the values of my family, my teammates, my friends, my sport, and the Australian Olympic team.
I’ve embarrassed you all.
I’m truly sorry,” he added.
Craig’s team were knocked out in the quarter-finals by the Netherlands on Sunday.
Australia gold!
Well, I have never seen that happen.
As Britain do their last changeover of rider at the front, Ethan Hayter slips off his saddle, though not off his bike.
That blows it for them because you lose speed with fewer riders.
Australia were already powering through the final lap and they win relatively comfortably, timed at 3:42.067 to GB’s 3:44.394.
No world record this time – that remains the 3:40.730 Australia rode earlier.
Their first gold in this race for 20 years.
Huge for their team of Oliver Bleddyn, Sam Welsford, Conor Leahy and Kelland O’Brien.
It’s four riders each.
They ride in groups on opposite sides of the track for 4km, trying to catch each other – hence “pursuit”.
Riders take turns in cycling at the front of their team, doing the hard work while the rest ride in the air pocket behind them.
Each time they cross the middle of the track, one team will be ahead of the other.
It could be by a matter of centimetres.
At halfway the green and gold lead, then after 3km the Brits are 0.2 sec ahead.
Over at the velodrome, Italy take bronze in the men’s team pursuit.
They won gold last time in Tokyo.
Now the gold medal race, Australia v Great Britain.
Eagerly awaited, this, because Australia dominated the discipline for years until Britain won Olympic gold in 2008, 2012 and 2016.
Australia qualified fastest in a world record and the word is they want to break it again here.
Hosts France earn the chance to challenge China in the table tennis men’s team semi-final after dispatching Brazil with a 3-0 win in the quarter-finals.
Alexis Lebrun teams up with Simon Gauzy to win the first doubles match in straight games before Felix Lebrun sees off Hugo Calderano, Brazil’s highest ranked player at world No 6.
Alexis then gets the third seeds over the finish line, beating Vitor Ishiy.
The celebrations begin for Li Fabin as his Olympic gold is confirmed.
Li retains his title after lifting a combined 310kg.
Morris fails in his brave world record bid, but records a total of 298kg to claim bronze.
Those two men sandwich Thai powerhouse Theerapong Silacahai, whose combined lifts of 303kg earn silver.
China’s Chen Yiwen and Chang Yani both qualify for the women’s 3m springboard semi-final.
The pair, who had already teamed up to win synchronized 3m gold, qualify first and fourth respectively.
Chen scores 356.40 points and Chang 308.75.
Australia’s Maddison Keeney and Mexico’s Aranza Vazquez finished second and third with scores of 337.35 and 321.75.
The semi-final is on Thursday at 4pm.
There is some seriously big lifting going on in South Paris Arena 6.
Hampton Morris points at the bar like it’s done something to affront him after lifting an Olympic record-equalling 172kg.
Silachai, meanwhile, clutches the Thai flag on his vest following a 171kg lift.
Li fails in his attempt at 172kg, but it matters not.
The only medals being disputed are silver and bronze.
Morris is going to have a pop at a world record 178kg.
China’s Guo Qing is ready for her -49kg taekwondo semi-final against Iran’s Mobina Nematzadeh.
The winner will face Thailand’s Panipak Wongpattanakit, who clinched her semi-final 2-0, in the gold medal match at 3.19am.
The loser will go into the bronze medal contest an hour earlier.
A rare mishap for Li Fabin as he records a no lift for his first attempt at 167kg in the clean and jerk.
You can’t keep a good man down, though.
He quickly returns for a second go and, with an effort that turns him red in the face, drags the bar high above his head.
Theerapong Sinachai then walks out and lifts 169kg.
He is second overall, behind Li, who comfortably outlifted the Thai in the snatch round.
Gold is as good as Li’s already.
The clean and jerk is going to be fairly short and sweet, given we’re down to eight athletes from the 12 who began the day.
There is some concern as Eko Irawan, who was second at halfway, hurts himself while desperately, and futilely, trying to avoid a third no lift.
Officials hastily erect a curtain to shield Irawan from view, but he is soon on his feet and being helped away by one of the Indonesian coaching staff.
Morea Baru of Papua New Guinea is leader in the clubhouse.
His combined total of 279kg is more than either of the other two athletes whose competitions have finished.
French world No 7 Celine Boutier is setting the pace on the opening day of the women’s golf tournament.
She is 7 under through 16 holes over at Le Golf National.
South Africa’s 2022 Open champion, Ashleigh Buhai, is 3 back at 4 under, with world No 2 Lilia Vu on 3 under.
China’s Janet Lin Xiu finished her round on 1 under, while compatriot Yin Ruoning went round in par.
Wang Manyu cruises to victory in the third match of the team quarter-final, beating Chinese Taipei’s Chien Tung-chuan 3-0.
That makes it 3-0 in matches to clinch the best-of-five tie.
China’s women book their berth in a semi-final against South Korea on Thursday.
Talk about asserting your supremacy over the field.
Li Fabin completes the snatch portion of the men’s 61kg weightlifting competition by lifting an Olympic record of 143kg.
He was last man to lift and duly attempted a heavier weight than any of his 11 rivals had tried.
The 137kg bar was easy-peasy for Li, and 140kg on his next go did not look much tougher.
Li was straining at 143kg but ultimately showed that bar who was boss.
Ahead of the clean and jerk, Eko Irawan of Indonesia is second after lifting 135kg.
Four men, including world silver medallist Sergio Massidda, are eliminated after recording three no lifts.
Gasps all around South Paris Arena 6 as world championship silver medallist Sergio Massidda records his third no lift for the snatch.
The Italian had one failed go at lifting 132kg, then two futile attempts to hoist 134kg.
Trinh Van Vinh is the second competitor to suffer a first round washout.
The Vietnamese’s third attempt to lift 128kg ended in unseemly fashion.
From a crouched position, the 28-year-old loses control and falls flat on his back.
Sergio Massida, who was second behind Li Fabin at last year’s world championship, fails on his first try at lifting 132kg.
Thailand’s Theerapong Silachai, however, flamboyantly gestures towards the 132kg bar he’s just firmly held above his head.
China women’s are one step away from securing a spot in the semi-finals of the team table tennis.
They lead Chinese Taipei 2-0, with Wang Manyu about to take on Chien Tung-chuan in the third match.
Wang and partner Chen Meng, the new Olympic champion, got China off to a fast start, winning their doubles against Chien Tung-chuan and Chen Szu-yu in straight games.
World No 1 Sun Yingsha then wins the second game against Cheng I-ching 11-9, 11-2, 11-8, and now it’s just down to Wang.
Over at Le Golf National, it’s the first day of women’s golf and we’ve got two early leaders, and a four-way tie for third.
France’s world No 7 Celine Boutier is leading at 4-under-par, with world No 2 Lilia Vu a short further back.
Mexico’s Gaby Lopez, India’s Dagar Diksha, Colombia’s Mariajo Uribe and South African’s Ashleigh Buhai are all tied at 2 under.
China’s Lin Xiyu is lurking three shots behind Boutier at 1 under, with Yin Ruoning holding par and tied for 12th.
An inconsolable John Ceniza buries his head in his hands, before being ushered away by a member of the Filipino coaching team, after recording his third no lift in the snatch round.
Ceniza had three pops at lifting 125kg but on each occasion barely got the bar off the floor.
Contrasting emotions for the demonstrative Morris, who releases an almighty scream and repeatedly punches the air after lifting 126kg.
Barring a late meltdown, Belgium look like booking their spot in the final four of the women’s basketball.
With 5:46 left in the fourth quarter they have a healthy 18 point lead.
Kyara Linskens leads the shooting with 19 points, while Antonia Delaere has contributed 13.
The USA’s Hampton Morris prowls around the bar, eyeing it with some contempt, before hoisting 122 kilograms of iron and steel above his head.
Morris leaves the stage waving and grinning from ear to ear.
Every seat in the 7,800 Paris 6 Arena is filled and the atmosphere is bubbling up nicely.
Finally, 37 minutes after the billed start time, the men’s 61kg weightlifting is under way.
We will keep you posted on events.
Li’s entrance is loudly acclaimed by a throng of Chinese supporters.
Wherever they compete in Paris, the country’s athletes are receiving tremendous backing from their compatriots.
Enough fun for now, however.
The 12 competitors get a 10-minute rest after emerging to wave at fans.
If you want an idea of how keen the crowd is to get into this, they are currently cheering 11 suited officials being announced to the crowd.
The Post is at Paris Arena 6 and waiting fairly patiently for the delayed men’s 61kg weightlifting competition to begin.
A voice over the PA triumphantly informs us we are five minutes from the athletes being introduced.
No reason given for the delay.
What we do know is, when the action gets going there is a very good chance of Chinese gold.
Li Fabin is the best in the business.
The 31-year-old is reigning Olympic, world and Asian Games champion and he will take some stopping here.
The women’s team table tennis quarter-final between China and Chinese Taipei is under way in Paris.
First up we have doubles action, with China’s Chen Meng and Wang Manyu, taking on Chen Szu-Yu and Chien Tung-Chuan.
Sun Yingsha and Wang are then in singles action, against Cheng I-Ching and Chien, respectively in the next two matches.
Should a fourth and fifth match be necessary, the teams will then choose who will play.
China’s Deng Lijuan took silver in the women’s speed climbing event in Paris, throwing in a personal best 6.18 seconds into the bargain.
Deng was almost perfect in the final three races of the competition, and says it was because she “didn’t think too much”.
“I was just focusing,” she says. “Every time I was out there, I tried to give my best.
During my last climb I couldn’t hear anything from the crowd.
I only focused on my climb.

China’s Li Fabin will begin the defence of his 61kg Olympic weightlifting title in about 15 minutes, and with a stack of world records to his name it would be hard to bet against him being successful.
In his first clean and jerk attempt in Tokyo, Li lifted his right leg off the ground while holding 166kg overhead, a signature position he sometimes takes to correct his balance.

Breaking makes its Olympic debut on Friday, and Mounir Baba, the China coach has been chatting about the “humility, discipline and will” that has made the country’s B-Girls and B-Boys so easy to train.
The Frenchman says it was “not hard at all” to get athletes to embrace breaking as a sport.
“They have been involved in break for more than 20 years,” he says. “This young generation is very talented.

A player on the Australian men’s hockey team was arrested in Paris and is being held in custody, the Australian Olympic Committee said on Wednesday, with the Paris prosecutor’s office saying he had been detained for buying cocaine.

“Police officers who witnessed a cocaine transaction at the foot of a building in the ninth arrondissement [of Paris], on the night of August 6 to 7, arrested the seller, born in December 2006, and the buyer, born in September 1995 in Australia,” the prosecutor’s office said.
Australia’s Olympic Committee said no charges had been laid against the member of the team, whose identity was not officially disclosed.
It did not comment on the reason for the arrest.
The SCMP’s video team have been taking a look at the thorny topic of how gender is defined in sports.
What are the standards of gender in sports and are they right?
What are the standards of gender in sports and are they right?
Cyclist Guo Yufang is through to the quarter-finals of the women’s Keirin after finishing second in Heat 3 of the first round.
The Chinese rider ends up 0.087 seconds back of Germany’s Emma Hinze, who wins the heat in 10.967 seconds.
To give you some indication of why China’s divers are top of the pile, here’s Wang Zongyuan on today’s performance, when he finished comfortably top in the semi-finals of the 3m springboard.
To put that into context, teammate Xie Siyi was second on 505.85 points and Great Britain’s Jack Laugher third on 467.05.
Track cyclist Harrie Lavreysen has posted a world record time of 9.088 seconds in the qualification round of the men’s sprint at the National Velodrome.
The Netherlands athlete hit an average speed of 79.225km/h in his run, leaving him just ahead of Australia’s Matthew Richardson (9.091) in second and Israel’s Mikhail Yakovlev (9.152) in third.
The previous world record was held by Trinidad and Tobago’s Paul Nicholas, who managed 9.100 in 2019.
China’s Zhou Yu qualified 18th with a time of 9.514, but teammate Liu Qui missed out after coming home in 9.904.
China’s Deng Lijuan claims silver in the inaugural women’s speed climbing event.

Deng scales the wall in a 6.18-second personal best in the big final – which decides the gold and silver medallists – but is eight hundredths of a second shy of her opponent, gold-medallist Aleksandra Miroslaw of Poland.
In the small final, Poland’s Aleksandra Kalucka romps past her opponent, Indonesia’s Rajiah Sallsabillah, by 1.71 seconds to take home the bronze medal.
Great Britain diver Jack Laugher has been talking about his performance in the semi-finals of the men’s 3m springboard.
Laugher finished third on 467.05 points, someway behind China’s Wang Zongyuan (537.85) and Xie Siyi (505.85).
“I’d love it to be me [to challenge the Chinese],” he says. “I try and do my best every time, and I am in admiration of how good they are.
Never really any doubt about this one, Australia were never in danger of losing, despite being outscored 19-13 in the final quarter.
Up next in the quarter-finals of the women’s basketball, it’s Spain against Belgium at 8.30pm.
Germany take on France at midnight, and then it’s the WNBA v Nigeria at 3.30am.
Over in the National Velodrome, where Hong Kong’s Ceci Lee Sze-wing will be in action on Sunday, it’s the qualifying round of the men’s sprint.
China’s Liu Qi is out first and posts a time of 9.904 seconds, which is quickly bettered.
Compatriot Zhou Yu goes fourth and hits 9.514.
Only another 26 riders to go.
Yang Jiayu has been talking about the penalties that ultimately cost her and partner Zhang Jun at shot at a medal in the marathon race walk mixed relay.
The pair were in second at one stage, but ultimately ended up well down the field in 15th.

“The first two legs, we had some advantage and were doing well, but we didn’t expect to be given so many penalties in the third leg.” Yang says. “In the final leg, when I took over, I didn’t think so much about chasing after a podium position.
“I just wanted to focus on having good technique, display a confident me.
After all, I won the gold medal in my individual event.
I wanted to show the Chinese spirit.
China have secured a spot in the table tennis men’s team semi-finals, by easily brushing aside South Korea in the last eight.
Ma Long and Wang Chuqin gets things off to a quick start, beating Cho Dae-seong and Jang Woo-jin in straight sets.
The reigning men’s singles champion Fan Zhendong continues his dominant run with a 3-1 victory over Korea’s Lim Jong-hoon.
Wang Chuqin then wraps up the tie with a 3-1 win over Jang Woo-jin.
In the latest of our video reviews from Paris, we take a look at China’s diving queen.
China’s 17-year-old diving queen has 3 Olympic golds, but who is Quan Hongchan?
China’s 17-year-old diving queen has 3 Olympic golds, but who is Quan Hongchan?
We’re well into the first quarter-final of the women’s basketball, and Australia are comfortably ahead with 5:12 left in the third quarter.
Alanna Smith leads the scores with 18 points, on 6-of-10 shooting.
The men’s 3m springboard semi-final wraps up at the Aquatics Centre, no surprise as both Chinese divers Wang and Xie both qualify, it’s news only if they don’t.
So here’s the list of 12 divers making it to the final tomorrow, we’ll be back for more splashes, or less.
The men’s 3m springboard semi-final is drawing to a close and, after five dives, China’s Wang is in a league of his own.
Xie recovers his poise following a couple of disappointing efforts to be awarded 88.8 points, his best score of the day, for a fine inward 3½ somersaults.
Wang adds another 86.4 points to his tally following his 3½ somersaults dive.
Laugher manages only 64.35 points for his forward 2½ somersaults 3 twists, a long way short of Wang’s exceptional 91.0.
It’s a reverse 3½ somersaults for both Xie and Wang on their fourth dive ... and Xie continues to trend in the wrong direction.
The reigning champion scores only 70.0.
No problem for 22-year-old Wang, though.
He is awarded 89.25 points for the 22-year-old.
After four rounds, Wang is first, followed by Xie and Laugher.
South Korean Haram Woo is fourth and Jordan Houlden of Great Britain fifth.
The top 12 qualify for tomorrow’s final.
China, with 22 golds, are aiming to claw back ground on the US (24) at the top of the Olympic medal table today.
The good news is, the Chinese have two likely podium toppers competing in today’s weightlifting.
The Post will be at South Paris Arena 6 to see if Li Fabin, the reigning world and Asian Games champion, can retain the title he won in Tokyo three years ago.
Li’s 61kg event begins at 9pm, and is followed at 1.30am by Hou Zhihui going for a second straight Olympic gold in the women’s 49kg competition.
Xie Siyi’s third attempt with a back 3½ somersaults gives him 81.0 points, the lowest of his three attempts so far.
Compatriot Wang Zongyuan’s forward 2½ somersaults 3 twists, a dive of 3.9 difficult degree and the highest for the Chinese today, scores him a 81.9 points, enough to cement his position at the top.
Jack Laugher though has a dive to forget in his third attempt.
His inward 3½ somersaults gives him only 69.7 points, and he is now down to the third, almost 16 points behind Wang.

After the excitement of Scottie Scheffler’s one-shot victory in the men’s golf, it is the turn of the woman to compete at Paris’s Le Golf National, the venue for Europe’s 2018 Ryder Cup thumping of the USA.
China’s 21-year-old major winner Yin Ruoning is 1-over-par after three holes, while compatriot Janet Lin Xiyu plays her opening two holes in 2 over.
Norway’s Celine Borge is the early front runner on 2 under through five.
In today’s first athletics event, China’s two teams finish 14th and 15th among 25 teams in the marathon race walk mixed relay.
China’s He Xianghong and Qieyang Shijie finish 14th place in a time of 2 hours, 59 minutes and 13 seconds, while teammates Zhang Jun and Yang Jiayu come home in 3:00:43.

Spain’s Alvaro Martin and Maria Perez take gold, finishing the 42.195km course in 2:50:31, 0.51s ahead of Brian Daniel Pintado and Glenda Morejon, who claimed Ecuador’s third silver medal in Games history.
Bronze goes to Australian duo Rhydian Cowley and Jemima Montag in 2:51:38.
The surfing is all over in Tahiti, but people are still talking about the final day of the competition on Monday.

A safe distance from athletes Tatiana Weston-Webb from Brazil and Brisa Hennessy of Costa Rica – who were competing in a semi-final match – a whale breached and gave spectators and photographers the Olympic moment of a lifetime.
It’s not uncommon for wild animals such as birds, seals and even sharks to appear while surfing around the world.
In Tahiti, where the 2024 Olympics surfing competition was held almost 10,000 miles way from the host city of Paris, whales gather around the islands during mating, birthing and migration season.
Wang surges to the top of the table with a 91.0 points reverse 1½ somersaults 3½ twists in his second attempt.
He now has a slender 3.5 points lead over Laugher of Great Britain.
It’s a reverse 3½ somersaults for Laugher’s second attempt of the day, a 87.5 point jump for the 2016 Rio de Janeiro Games silver medallist.
Xie doesn’t do better than him with his reverse 2½ somersaults 1½ twists, which only score 84.15 points.
Further down the table, Mexican diver Olvera Ibarra’s second attempt with a reverse 3½ somersaults lands him a much lower score of 68.25, after scoring 81.6 with his first.
But there’s quite some improvement for Germany’s Moritz Wesemann, his forward 2½ somersaults 2 twists in his second attempt lands him 81.60 points, a massive jump from his 66.3 points first effort.
Another Chinese pair, Qin Weibo and Xu Zhuoyi race in tonight’s men’s 100m hurdles semi-finals.
In the men’s 200m semi-finals, from 2.02am, Noah Lyles will continue his bid to claim the sprint double after the American’s 100m triumph on Sunday.
Great Britain’s Matthew Hudson-Smith and Quincy Hall of the US are favourites for the men’s 400m title.
The gold medal race is at 3.20am.
The men’s team table tennis quarter-final between China and South Korea is now under way.
China’s Ma Long and Wang Chuqin get a quick win in men’s doubles against Cho Dae-seong and Jang Woo-jin, winning 11-5, 11-9 and 11-5.
Fan Zhendong, the men’s singles gold medallist, will face Lim Jong-hoon, with Wang battling Jang in the following two matches of singles.
As we said, she talks a good game.
The morning’s athletics is up and running at a scorching Stade de France, and it is not good news for China’s Wu Yanni.
The 27-year-old is sixth in her 100m hurdles heat in a time of 12.97 seconds.
Wu can count her blessings for the introduction of repechage rounds at this Olympics.
She gets a second chance to reach the semi-finals in 24 hours.
Xie’s first dive is a forward 2½ somersaults 2 twists, of difficult degree 3.4, and the reigning champion scores 85.0 for his effort.
Wang performs an inward 3½ somersaults, also of difficult degree 3.4, and scores 86.7 to share the top spot with Jack Laugher of Great Britain after the first round.
Xie is in third place while Osmar Olvera Ibarra is also in contention for a podium place after his 81.6 points dive in the opening round.
At the Aquatics Centre, the men’s 3m springboard semi-final is under way.
Twelve divers have had their first attempt, while China’s Xie Siyi and Wang Zongyuan will be the last two to jump in this 18-strong field.
Jonathan Ruvalcaba of Dominican Republic tops the table early.

Wang and Xi, silver and gold medallists from the Tokyo Games, topped the preliminary table with 530.65 and 509.60 points respectively, more than 40 points above third overall Jack Laugher of Great Britain, and are largely in a league of the own.
Chinese sprint canoeist Wang Nan directly qualifies to the semi-finals in the women’s kayak single 500m after coming first in her heat, with a time of 1 minute 51.28 seconds.
Compatriot Yin Mengdie, meanwhile, is through to the quarter-finals after finishing fourth in her heat in 1:52.29.
The fastest two in each heat qualify for the semi-finals, and third to seventh fastest the quarter-finals.
